title: Perf suite release gating proposal (runtime) — draft
body:
Context
- Project: “Perf baseline & representative workload suite” (Q1 2026).
- This doc proposes how the perf suite becomes a first-class release gate for the serving runtime (redwood repo) without blocking day-to-day development due to normal variance.
- Primary goals:
  1) Detect meaningful regressions early (PR-level where feasible).
  2) Make release-candidate signoff predictable and repeatable.
  3) Provide a clear exception + escalation path that prevents “perf gate fatigue.”

Non-goals (for this proposal)
- Publishing external benchmarks.
- Replacing correctness/quality gates.
- Building an entirely new CI system (this assumes existing CI + perf-canary plumbing).

Definitions (to align on wording)
- Workload suite: v1 representative workloads (chat streaming, long-context prefill/summarization, tool/function calling bursts, embeddings high-QPS).
- Metrics: TTFT (time-to-first-token), TPOT (time-per-output-token), throughput (tokens/s, req/s where appropriate). Percentiles: p50/p95/p99.
- “Noise”: expected variance due to cluster conditions, clocks, placement, etc. Governed by perf regression policy thresholds.
- “Regression”: metric change beyond the configured threshold AND repeatable (per policy / minimum samples).
- “Gating mode”: perf job whose failure blocks merge (PR) or blocks release promotion (release branch).

Current state (as of late Jan / early Feb)
- Representative suite exists in benchmark-lab and is wired into perf-canary nightly (PR perf-canary#21562).
- Runtime instrumentation improvements are landing (scheduler queue/batch metrics, kernel selection dumps), enabling attribution.
- We have a baseline anchor build for Q1 2026 (see Slack eng-runtime thread on baseline freeze date).
- Open issue: we are still calibrating variance by SKU/region; thresholds may need per-workload/per-SKU adjustments.

Proposal overview
We implement a 3-tier model:
1) PR-level “smoke perf” (fast + stable) — blocks merges to main for runtime changes.
2) Nightly representative suite (broad coverage) — does not block merges but pages/alerts on confirmed regressions and creates release risk signals.
3) Release-branch “gating” (full suite) — blocks release promotion unless explicitly waived by Runtime Lead + SRE Integration Lead.

Tier 1: PR-level smoke perf (merge gate)
Objective
- Catch obvious perf cliffs (e.g., kernel fallback, scheduler changes causing large TTFT spikes) within ~20–40 minutes.

What runs
- Hardware/regions: 1 SKU + 1 region initially (recommend: H100 in us-east; alternate A100 depending on fleet stability).
- Workloads (subset):
  - Chat streaming: 1 mix, moderate concurrency, short-to-medium prompt bins; streaming enabled.
  - Long-context prefill: 1 config representing “large prefill / modest decode” (KV pressure).
  - Optional: embeddings micro-benchmark if runtime change touches embed path or shared components.
- Model set (subset): top 1–2 models per family OR (more realistic) the top 2 deployed overall.
  - Recommendation for v1 PR gate: 2 models total, chosen for coverage (one Llama-family, one Qwen-family or Mistral-family).

How it gates
- Compare PR results to baseline anchor (Q1 2026) OR to last-green on main for the same job definition.
- Gating thresholds (initial recommendations; will be tuned per noise model):
  - TTFT p99: fail if regression > +7% AND absolute delta > +25ms.
  - TPOT p95: fail if regression > +5%.
  - Throughput: fail if regression < -5%.
- Minimum sampling:
  - At least N=3 runs (or 3 shards) and require 2/3 agreement on regression direction to fail.
  - Warmup standardized per benchmark-lab doc (avoid first-run cold-start artifacts).

Pass/fail behavior
- If the PR perf job fails:
  - PR is blocked from merge.
  - CI posts a summary comment with:
    - metric deltas
    - run manifest IDs
    - link to dashboard panel
    - suggested next action (rerun vs investigate)

Reruns
- Allowed rerun budget: 2 reruns per PR automatically if failure is within “gray zone” (see below).
- If still failing, require owner to:
  - confirm whether change is expected, and
  - either fix regression or request waiver (waivers are disallowed for PR gate except for infra flakiness; see exceptions).

Tier 2: Nightly representative suite (signal + alerting)
Objective
- Broad coverage on realistic traffic shapes; catch drift that PR smoke perf doesn’t.

What runs
- Hardware/regions:
  - Minimum: us-east + eu-west.
  - SKUs: H100 + A100, and L40S where applicable for relevant models.
- Full representative workload suite v1.
- Model matrix: top deployed models per family + any high-growth catalog additions. Keep bounded (we should publish/maintain a nightly matrix rather than letting it sprawl).

How it alerts (non-blocking)
- Alerts in triage channel when:
  - Confirmed regression exceeds threshold AND persists across 2 consecutive nightlies.
  - Regression affects release-branch candidates (see Tier 3 link below).
- Paging policy: Only page (on-call) for severe regressions likely to impact prod SLOs, e.g.:
  - TTFT p99 +15% (or +75ms) on chat streaming cohort
  - Throughput -10% sustained on embeddings high-QPS
  - Any “latency cliff” correlated with kernel fallback or scheduler overload mode

Output
- Nightly generates:
  - dashboard entries tagged nightly build SHA
  - run manifests (schema per ADR-0172)
  - optional profiling artifacts when anomaly detection triggers (future; not required for first pass)

Tier 3: Release-branch gating (promotion gate)
Objective
- Prevent shipping a runtime release with a meaningful perf regression relative to baseline / previous release.

What runs
- Full suite v1 (same as nightly), but on a pinned environment with higher isolation:
  - dedicated benchmark windows
  - clock locking where allowed
  - reduced co-tenancy
- Run against candidate runtime build tag (release branch) and compare to:
  - last release tag baseline, and
  - Q1 2026 baseline anchor (for overall drift tracking)

How it gates
- Release promotion is blocked if regression thresholds exceed policy.
- Exception requires explicit waiver (see “Exception policy” below) and must be documented in release notes.

Gray zone handling (noise-aware gating)
We need a principled middle area between “pass” and “fail” to avoid thrash:
- Green: within threshold.
- Gray: slightly over threshold but within expected noise bounds OR inconsistent across shards.
- Red: clearly over threshold and consistent.

Operationally:
- PR gate should treat Gray as “rerun automatically” once; if still Gray, escalate to “needs perf triage” label and block merge until triaged.
- Nightly should treat Gray as “track” (no alert) unless it persists >3 days or trends worsen.
- Release gate should treat Gray as “requires human signoff” (Runtime lead + SRE) before promotion.

Exception policy (when gates can be bypassed)
Allowed exceptions (and who can approve)
1) Infra flakiness / benchmark fleet incident
  - Signals: widespread failures across unrelated PRs; SRE confirms instability; or INT/Jira ticket opened.
  - Approval: SRE Integration Lead (Sean Gallagher) OR on-call SRE.
  - Documentation: link to incident/ticket + rerun plan.

2) Intentional tradeoff
  - Example: throughput improvement at the cost of small TTFT increase, or long-prefill optimized at slight chat cost.
  - Approval: Runtime org lead (Mateo Alvarez) + Applied ML sponsor if quality-related (Dr. Maya Srinivasan delegate).
  - Documentation: brief writeup in PR + follow-up task to update baselines/thresholds if this becomes the new expected behavior.

3) Known issue with tracking bug
  - Example: kernel auto-selection mis-picks on a specific SKU; we pin kernel for baseline runs while fix is in progress.
  - Approval: Runtime lead + owner of subsystem (e.g., Hiro Tanaka for kernels).
  - Documentation: tracking ticket + explicit scope of impact + expiry date for the waiver.

Disallowed exceptions
- “It’s probably fine” without attribution.
- Waiving PR smoke perf because it’s inconvenient (unless infra is confirmed broken).

Escalation + triage path
When a regression is detected (PR, nightly, or release gate):
1) Confirm measurement boundary
  - Validate manifest: region, SKU, driver/CUDA, runtime build, scheduler config, cache mode (cold/warm), workload seed.
  - Confirm TTFT/TPOT definitions match canonical (Slack debate; ADR-0172 boundaries).

2) Reproduce
  - Rerun same manifest on stable benchmark window.
  - If repro fails, classify as noise and update noise model notes (Drive scratchpad).

3) Attribute
  - Check scheduler metrics: queue wait, batch assembly time, batch size distributions.
  - Check kernel selection debug dump: selected kernel, fallback reason, sequence-length regime.
  - If needed, follow profiling playbook to capture traces.

4) Decide action
  - Fix forward in PR.
  - Revert change (if urgent and regression is clear).
  - Waive with documented tradeoff + follow-up.

Ownership
- Primary owner for gating integration: Connor O’Brien.
- CI reliability and GPU pipeline: Sahana Iyer.
- Benchmark harness correctness and job definitions: Rina Kobayashi.
- Methodology/thresholding: Claire Dubois + Sana Farid (noise model).
- Alert routing + on-call policy: Sean Gallagher + Aisha Bello.

Implementation plan (proposed milestones)
Milestone A — PR smoke perf (2–3 weeks)
- Define job spec (models/workloads/SKU/region) and keep it stable.
- Add CI job that:
  - builds runtime artifact
  - runs benchmark-lab harness
  - uploads results + manifest
  - posts PR comment
- Add pass/fail comparator with threshold config in repo (versioned).

Milestone B — Nightly suite hardened (parallel)
- Ensure nightly runs are consistent across regions.
- Add “confirmed regression” detection across consecutive runs.
- Wire alert severity rules (page vs triage channel).

Milestone C — Release branch gating
- Add explicit “release candidate perf gate” workflow triggered on release branch.
- Add waiver mechanism requiring named approvals.
- Add release note template section for perf waivers.

Milestone D — Tighten coverage (post-v1)
- Expand PR smoke set if runtime changes frequently impact a path not covered.
- Add per-SKU thresholds if needed.
- Add automated “suspect commit” bisection hooks (nice-to-have).

Open questions / TODO
- Finalize which SKU is most stable for PR gating (H100 vs A100 vs L40S). SRE input needed based on fleet variance.
- Decide whether PR smoke perf compares to:
  - baseline anchor (static), or
  - last-green main (rolling). Static is simpler, rolling tracks drift.
- How to handle caching scenarios:
  - Decision trending: report both cold and warm (prefix/KV cache). For gating: likely cold for determinism + optional warm for realism.
- How to handle model version pinning:
  - We should pin model weights + tokenizer revisions for gating. Any model update requires explicit baseline refresh.
- Threshold calibration:
  - Need concrete per-workload variance numbers before locking thresholds; use early Q1 sweeps.

Appendix: Proposed PR smoke perf job spec (initial strawman)
- Region/SKU: us-east / H100
- Models: (TBD) 1 Llama-family + 1 Qwen/Mistral-family
- Workloads:
  - chat_streaming_v1: concurrency=32, prompt bins short/med, decode distribution variable
  - long_prefill_v1: prefill ~8k–16k tokens, decode ~256–512, concurrency=8
- Metrics gate: TTFT p99, TPOT p95, throughput

Appendix: What will show up in the PR comment
- Summary table: baseline vs PR
- Links:
  - dashboard (panel filtered by PR SHA)
  - run manifest JSON
  - kernel selection dump (if enabled)
  - scheduler metrics breakdown

Notes to self (Connor)
- Keep the PR gate small and boring. If we try to include the full suite in PR CI we will either (a) go broke on GPU hours or (b) disable it after 2 weeks.
- The value is not just detecting regressions; it’s forcing fast attribution. Instrumentation links are part of the “product.”
